links.comparator_used: Original model before retraining (model not updated after deployment), with performance compared at fixed 90% sensitivity
links.outcome: Specificity of the mortality prediction model at fixed 90% sensitivity after retraining on EHR data affected by model use
links.effect: Mortality model lost 9% to 39% specificity after retraining once; a mortality model created after an AKI model was implemented lost 8% to 15% specificity; simultaneous AKI and mortality models reduced each other's effective accuracy by 1% to 28%
links.tradeoff: Retraining on data shaped by model-driven interventions degraded performance. No universally effective model-updating approach was found, and model use may need to be recorded to keep models viable.
links.quote: At fixed 90% sensitivity, in scenario 1 a mortality prediction model lost 9% to 39% specificity after retraining once and in scenario 2 a mortality prediction model lost 8% to 15% specificity when created after the implementation of an acute kidney injury (AKI) prediction model; in scenario 3, models for AKI and mortality prediction implemented simultaneously, each led to reduced effective accuracy of the other by 1% to 28%.

design_hint: model retraining and update strategies (drift monitoring/recalibration)
